name: The Decision Rights Map
unit: a team that shares recurring decisions

flow.does: The recurring decisions this team actually makes
One decider, a consulted list, an informed list
Circle contested, blank, absent or group-owned rows
Name one owner out loud and say what changes

commitment: The decision that was contested, blank, absent or “the team”
Its single owner, named out loud
What changes now that it has one name
What the owner must still consult before moving
debrief_prompts: How many rows have a name you expected, and how many surprised you?
Which person appears on every row — is that clarity or a bottleneck?
Which rows have nobody willing to admit they own it?
Where does the real decider differ from the org chart?
For the circled row: was the ambiguity about who decides, or whether it should be a decision at all?
How will we notice in a month that the pen actually moved?
watch_outs: Nobody will claim a decision — ask who lives with the consequence.
Everyone wants the important one — ask what they would give to not own it.
It collapses into a committee — force a single name; consultation stays open.
note: No pre/post measure in this folder: the artifact is the point. Hand this spec to an agent to render a fillable sheet or a live form.
